label: Melanoma_Invasive_Overview_NOS
answer_markdown:
## Key Facts
- Invasive melanoma affects deeper skin layers, often presenting as asymmetrical lesions.
- Key histologic features: asymmetry, pagetoid scatter, and lack of maturation with depth.
- Essential staging criteria: Breslow thickness, mitotic rate, and presence of ulceration.
- Common genetic mutations: BRAF and NRAS.
- Prognosis depends on subtype and staging factors.

## Terminology
- Invasive melanoma: a malignant tumor derived from melanocytes.
- Synonyms: Malignant melanoma, Melanocytic neoplasm.

## Essential and Desirable Diagnostic Criteria
- **Essential:**
  - Asymmetry, lack of maturation with depth, pagetoid scatter of melanocytes.
  - Deep and atypical mitoses, ulceration.
  - Breslow thickness, mitotic rate, ulceration [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanoma.html).
- **Desirable:**
  - Genetic testing may reveal mutations such as BRAF or NRAS.

## Etiology/Pathogenesis
- Mutations in BRAF and NRAS are common.
- Associated with UV exposure, except for acral and mucosal types.
  - Acral melanoma often occurs on palms and soles.
  - Desmoplastic melanoma is often nonpigmented and may mimic scars [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanoma.html).

## Clinical Issues
- **Epidemiology:** 
  - More common in fair-skinned individuals.
  - Occurrence peaks in middle age.
- **Natural History:** 
  - Potential for metastasis if not caught early.
- **Prognosis:**
  - Depends on Breslow thickness, ulceration, and mitotic rate.
  - Sentinel lymph node involvement is a critical prognostic factor.

## Macroscopic
- Typically presents as a pigmented lesion.
- May show ulceration or nodular growths.

## Microscopic
- Asymmetrical with poorly defined borders.
- Pagetoid scatter and atypical melanocytes [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/SKIN/Melanoma_Metastatic_To_The_Skin.html).
- Common features across subtypes: 
  - Superficial spreading, nodular, lentigo maligna, acral lentiginous, desmoplastic [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticmelanoma.html).
- Presence of mitotic figures and absence of maturation.

![Superficial spreading melanoma](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/imgau/skintumormelanocyticmelanomadonati01.jpg)

## Ancillary Tests
- **IHC Panel:**
  - S100 positive, HMB45, Melan-A.
  - SOX10 often positive [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/SKIN/Dermal_Melanoma.html).
- **Molecular/Genetics:**
  - BRAF mutations common in various subtypes.

## Differential Diagnosis
- **Halo Nevus:**
  - Lack of severe atypia and ulceration [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/SKIN/Halo_Naevus.html).
- **Recurrent Nevus:**
  - More regular architecture [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/SKIN/Recurrent_Naevus.html).
- **Nodular Melanoma:**
  - Homogenous nodular growth compared to varied architectural patterns [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/skintumormelanocyticnodularmelanoma.html).
- **Melanoma Metastatic to the Skin:**
  - Difficult to distinguish from primary melanoma; presence of atypical cells and mitoses [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/SKIN/Melanoma_Metastatic_To_The_Skin.html).
- **Mucosal Melanoma:**
  - Involves mucous membranes, can be confused with primary cutaneous versions [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/SKIN/Mucosal_Melanoma.html).

cards.title: Melanoma metastatic to the skin
cards.excerpt: Entity: Melanoma metastatic to the skin definition: Metastatic melanoma in the skin is melanoma that has spread from a primary melanoma (cutaneous or extracutaneous) to the skin. related_terminology: None essential_and_desirable_diagnostic_criteria: Essential: an intradermal or subcutaneous nodule of malignant neoplastic melanocytes. Desirable: a history of melanoma; immunohistochemical and/or molecular confirmation in challenging cases; cytological, immunohistochemical, and genetic features similar to those of primary melanoma.

cards.title: Dermal melanoma
cards.excerpt: Entity: Dermal melanoma Section: ancillary_studies Neoplastic melanocytes express melanocytic markers, including melan-A, SOX10, HMB45, and S100.

cards.title: Naevoid melanoma
cards.excerpt: Entity: Naevoid melanoma Section: ancillary_studies The immunohistochemistry is similar to that of low-CSD melanoma.

cards.title: Halo naevus
cards.excerpt: Entity: Halo naevus Section: differential_diagnosis The differential diagnosis of involuting halo naevi includes other lichenoid interface reactions, such as those seen in lichenoid keratosis and melanoma with lichenoid inflammation. Findings suggestive of melanoma include the presence of a separate population of cells with an expansile pattern of growth; severe cytological atypia; and frequent mitoses, ulceration, or tumour necrosis. The halo phenomenon may occasionally involve other types of naevi, including dysplastic, Spitz, and congenital naevi, as well as melanomas. In most lesions, there is no intraepidermal melanocytic proliferation adjacent to the dermal component. If in situ or superficially invasive melanoma is present adjacent to a dermal lesion simulating halo naevus, the entire lesion is most likely melanoma.

cards.title: Recurrent naevus
cards.excerpt: Entity: Recurrent naevus Section: differential_diagnosis The histological differential diagnosis includes melanoma, dysplastic naevus, sclerosing naevus, and dysplastic naevus with florid fibroplasia.

cards.title: Mucosal melanoma
cards.excerpt: Entity: Mucosal melanoma Section: differential_diagnosis The differential diagnosis includes dysplastic naevi and special-site naevi (see section Dysplastic naevus, and section Special-site naevi (of the breast, axilla, scalp, and ear)).

cards.title: Melanoma metastatic to the skin
cards.excerpt: Entity: Melanoma metastatic to the skin Section: differential_diagnosis The histological differential diagnosis of metastatic melanoma in the skin includes primary melanoma, primary dermal melanoma, and atypical naevus. Blue naevus–like metastases are difficult to distinguish from common or epithelioid blue naevus. The presence of cytologically atypical epithelioid melanocytes and mitotic figures can mimic blue naevus–like melanoma.

cards.title: Nodular melanoma
cards.excerpt: Entity: Nodular melanoma Section: differential_diagnosis Unpigmented tumours must be distinguished from squamous cell carcinomas, appendageal tumours, sarcomas, and cutaneous lymphomas by immunohistochemistry. Melanoma metastases tend to have more mitoses or intravascular deposits of neoplastic melanocytes at the base.

cards.title: Invasive melanoma — Pathophysiology
cards.excerpt:
Multistep process that involves interaction of genomic, environmental and host factors
4 step model proposed (Pigment Cell Melanoma Res 2016;29:122)
Mitogenic driver mutation (i.e., BRAF mutation)
Escaping primary senescence (i.e., CDKN2A loss)
Overcoming apoptosis (i.e., TP53 mutation)
Immortalization (i.e., TERTp mutation)

cards.title: Invasive melanoma — Diagnosis
cards.excerpt:
Total body skin examination for the identification of clinically suspicious lesions (J Am Acad Dermatol 2019;80:208)
Histopathological diagnosis after wide surgical excision is the gold standard (J Am Acad Dermatol 2019;80:208, Eur J Cancer 2025;215:115152)
Correlation with clinical parameters, including age, gender, anatomical location and dermoscopic findings (Arch Dermatol 2005;141:434)
